### Troubleshooting already performed

`codex exec ... "say hello"` should complete using the authenticated ChatGPT subscription.

items.title: ChatGPT-authenticated Codex repeatedly reconnects and previously returned 401 with unexpected sk-svcac credential

items.body: ## Summary Codex CLI 0.157.0 running in GitHub Codespaces repeatedly fails with: 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: ...... This occurs even though Codex is explicitly configured for ChatGPT authentication, `codex login status` reports "Logged in using ChatGPT", the ChatGPT OAuth tokens are present and recently refreshed, and no OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY is configured in the shell or Codex app-server processes. The credential reported by the 401 (`...`) cannot be found in any active configuration/environment source I have identified. This appears to be an authentication-source/routing issue rather than an invalid user-supplied API key. ## Environment - Codex CLI: 0.157.0 - Environment: GitHub Codespaces - OS: Linux / Codespaces - Model: GPT-6-Sol - Reasoning effort: high - Authentication method: ChatGPT - Account shown by Codex: Pro Lite - Repository/workspace: `/workspaces/trading-operations-console` - Codex server: Local background server - Model provider shown by `/status`: openai - Permissions: Workspace (Approve for me) ## Expected behavior When Codex is authenticated using ChatGPT OAuth and: `codex login status` returns: `Logged in using ChatGPT` Codex should use the authenticated ChatGPT credentials when sending requests to: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` No unrelated API-key credential should override or replace the ChatGPT OAuth credentials. A simple prompt should complete successfully. ## Actual behavior A minimal prompt such as: `Reply with exactly: AUTH_OK` `Do not inspect files, run commands, use tools, or make any changes.` repeatedly fails after retries with: `401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: ...` against: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` The error persists across newly created Codex sessions. ## Authentication state `codex login status` returns: `Logged in using ChatGPT` `~/.codex/auth.json` reports: - `auth_mode: chatgpt` - `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not present - OAuth token fields are present: - access_token - id_token - refresh_token - account_id - `last_refresh` updates after authentication I did NOT include token values in this report. ## Configuration Relevant safe lines from `~/.codex/config.toml`: preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt" model = "gpt-6-sol" model_reasoning_effort = "high" service_tier = "default" The project is configured as trusted. ## Environment-variable diagnostics The current shell contains no OPENAI_API_KEY or CODEX_API_KEY. The Codex/app-server process environments were inspected. They contain Codex internal/package variables but no: - OPENAI_API_KEY - OPENAI_API_KEY_FILE - CODEX_API_KEY Therefore I have not identified an environment API key overriding the ChatGPT login. ## Active-file credential search I searched active Codex/config/shell/Codespaces configuration files for the prefix of the credential appearing in the 401 response. No active configuration file containing that credential was found. The prefix appears only in historical Codex session/rollout JSONL files where previous 401 errors were recorded. Those files appear to contain the error history, not an active credential source. ## Background processes Running processes include the Codex managed app-server and its daemon pid-update loop. Inspection of their environments did not reveal an OpenAI or Codex API key. Restarting the Codex app-server did not resolve the issue. ## Troubleshooting already performed I have: 1. Logged out/re-authenticated with ChatGPT. 2. Confirmed `codex login status` says "Logged in using ChatGPT". 3. Confirmed OAuth tokens exist in `~/.codex/auth.json`. 4. Confirmed `OPENAI_API_KEY` is absent. 5. Confirmed `OPENAI_API_KEY_FILE` is absent. 6. Confirmed `CODEX_API_KEY` is absent. 7. Forced `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt"`. 8. Restarted Codex. 9. Restarted the managed Codex app-server. 10. Started fresh Codex sessions. 11. Inspected the app-server process environment. 12. Searched active config files for the credential prefix reported in the 401. 13. Repeated the test using a minimal prompt requiring no tools or repository access. The failure remains reproducible. ## Reproduction steps 1. Start a GitHub Codespace. 2. Run Codex CLI 0.157.0. 3. Authenticate using "Sign in with ChatGPT". 4. Verify: `codex login status` returns: `Logged in using ChatGPT` 5. Verify `/status` shows the expected ChatGPT account/session. 6. Send: `Reply with exactly: AUTH_OK` 7. Codex retries the request. 8. Request fails with: `401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...` 9. Error references: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` ## Additional observation During troubleshooting there were also transient messages such as: `Stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed` followed by reconnect attempts. The terminal ultimately returns the same 401 incorrect-API-key error. ## Why this appears abnormal The visible authentication state and the credential actually referenced by the backend appear inconsistent: Visible/local state: - ChatGPT authentication - valid OAuth token structure - login status reports ChatGPT - no API-key environment variable - no API-key credential found in active configuration Backend error: - reports an `sk-svcac...` API credential I would expect either: 1. the ChatGPT OAuth credentials to be used, or 2. Codex to clearly identify the configuration source overriding them. Instead the CLI reports ChatGPT authentication while requests appear to be evaluated using a different credential. ## Possibly related issues There have been other Codex reports involving 401 failures despite ChatGPT login, including cases involving auth headers, refresh-token handling, or credential-source precedence. My case differs in an important way: environment-variable inspection and active-file searches have not identified the `...` credential reported by the backend. ## Security No full API keys, OAuth access tokens, refresh tokens, ID tokens, account IDs, or other credentials are intentionally included in this report. Any credential appearing in screenshots/logs should be treated as sensitive and redacted before publication.

items.title: Codex CLI 0.157.0 uses unexpected sk-svcac credential and returns 401 despite valid ChatGPT OAuth login

items.body:
### Summary

Codex successfully authenticates using ChatGPT OAuth and `codex doctor` reports no stored API key, but inference requests fail after WebSocket retries/fallback with:

```
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...[redacted]...fvMA
```

Endpoint: `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

This reproduces across Codex CLI 0.153.4, 0.156.1, and 0.157.0 and, critically, with a completely fresh `CODEX_HOME` followed by a fresh ChatGPT OAuth login.

### Environment

- macOS 27.2.0, Apple Silicon / aarch64
- iTerm2 3.6.11
- ChatGPT Pro
- Current Codex CLI 0.157.0
- Provider: openai
- Authentication: ChatGPT OAuth
- Proxy: none

### Diagnostics

`codex login status`:

```
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

`codex doctor --json` reports:

```
auth.credentials: ok
stored API key: false
stored ChatGPT tokens: true
stored auth mode: chatgpt
```

Provider reachability is OK, and the Responses WebSocket diagnostic succeeds with `HTTP 101 Switching Protocols`, `auth mode: chatgpt`.

No `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` authentication environment variables are set.

### Reproduction

From a trusted Git repository:

```bash
codex exec "Reply with exactly: CODEX_OK"
```

Observed sequence:

```
WebSocket reconnects
warning: Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport.
stream disconnected before completion: websocket closed by server before response.completed
HTTPS reconnects
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...[redacted]...fvMA
```

### Version matrix

| CLI | Auth | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.157.0 | ChatGPT OAuth | 401 |
| 0.156.1 | ChatGPT OAuth | 401 |
| 0.153.4 | ChatGPT OAuth | 401 |
| 0.157.0, fresh CODEX_HOME | fresh ChatGPT OAuth | 401 |

### Fresh CODEX_HOME reproduction

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-isolated
chmod 700 /tmp/codex-isolated
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-isolated codex login
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-isolated codex login status
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-isolated codex doctor --json
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-isolated codex exec "Reply with exactly: CODEX_ISOLATED_OK"
```

OAuth login succeeds. The isolated doctor result is `overallStatus: ok` and reports:

```
auth file: /private/tmp/codex-isolated/auth.json
stored API key: false
stored ChatGPT tokens: true
stored auth mode: chatgpt
config.toml: missing
MCP servers: 0
active rollout files: 0
Responses WebSocket handshake succeeded
auth mode: chatgpt
handshake result: HTTP 101 Switching Protocols
```

The isolated inference still returns the same 401 and the same masked `sk-svcac...[redacted]...fvMA` credential.

### Request IDs

- 0.157.0: `1add0ef3-8195-423d-83f5-217cfe037bd4`
- 0.156.1: `f30bffa2-846e-4588-9dae-df49398401fa`
- 0.153.4: `a307b5bd-177d-49d4-9d50-46b0956fc539`
- 0.157.0 + fresh CODEX_HOME/OAuth: `d7fdd504-16c7-41b6-a31f-0adaf6d9632f`

Isolated reproduction CF-Ray: `a40ddcaa9fc46be3-DFW`

### Expected behavior

After successful ChatGPT OAuth authentication, Codex inference should complete using the authenticated ChatGPT account.

### Actual behavior

OAuth setup and WebSocket handshake succeed, but the inference stream closes before `response.completed`. After retries and HTTPS fallback, `/backend-api/codex/responses` returns 401 and identifies an `sk-svcac...` credential as an incorrect API key.

The same masked credential appears after a completely fresh `CODEX_HOME` and fresh OAuth login while Codex explicitly reports `stored API key: false`.

### Security

OAuth/access/refresh tokens, account ID, and the full rejected credential are intentionally omitted.

items.title: Unable to use codex due to API "service key"?

items.body:
## Summary

Codex Desktop and standalone Codex CLI fail on every model request with:

```text
Unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...
url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

This occurs even though Codex reports `Logged in using ChatGPT`. I am using a ChatGPT Pro subscription and am not using API-key authentication.

I reproduced the issue with both the Codex version bundled with the desktop app and the current standalone Codex CLI. I also reproduced it using a completely clean `CODEX_HOME` followed by a fresh ChatGPT OAuth login.

Importantly, manually sending the OAuth `access_token` and `account_id` from the resulting `auth.json` to the same `/backend-api/codex/responses` endpoint gets past authentication and returns HTTP 400 rather than 401.

This suggests the OAuth token/account itself is accepted by the backend, but the credential used by Codex for the model request is different. The Codex 401 specifically reports an unexpected `sk-svcac...` credential.

No API key matching that credential can be found in the Codex configuration, auth file, shell environment, launchd environment, or shell startup files.

## Environment

- macOS
- ChatGPT Pro
- Authentication: Sign in with ChatGPT
- Codex Desktop bundled CLI: `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.4`
- Standalone Codex CLI: `codex-cli 0.157.0`

Both versions reproduce the problem.

## Authentication state

`codex login status` returns:

```text
Logged in using ChatGPT
```

Metadata-only inspection of `~/.codex/auth.json` shows:

```text
auth.json exists: True
top-level keys: ['auth_mode', 'OPENAI_API_KEY', 'tokens', 'last_refresh']
auth_mode: chatgpt
has OPENAI_API_KEY: False
has tokens: True
token keys: ['id_token', 'access_token', 'refresh_token', 'account_id']
has access_token: True
has refresh_token: True
has account_id: True
```

The token was freshly refreshed during troubleshooting. No token values or account IDs are included here.

## Environment-variable checks

`echo $OPENAI_API_KEY` returns nothing.

```bash
env | grep -E '^(OPENAI|CODEX)_'
```

also returns nothing.

The following return nothing:

```bash
launchctl getenv OPENAI_API_KEY
launchctl getenv CODEX_API_KEY
launchctl getenv CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN
```

No `sk-svcac` credential was found in shell startup files.

## Reproduction with bundled Codex

Running:

```bash
/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex
```

and entering:

```text
Reply with exactly: TEST OK
```

results in HTTP 401 from `https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses` with an error stating:

```text
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...
```

The bundled binary reports `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.4`.

## Reproduction with standalone Codex

Standalone `codex-cli 0.157.0` reports `Logged in using ChatGPT`, but the same TEST OK prompt produces the same 401 and unexpected `sk-svcac...` credential error.

## Clean CODEX_HOME reproduction

To rule out configuration, plugins, MCP servers, hooks, sessions, and other normal `~/.codex` state:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/codex-clean-test
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-clean-test ~/.local/bin/codex login
```

I completed a fresh ChatGPT browser OAuth login.

```bash
CODEX_HOME=/tmp/codex-clean-test ~/.local/bin/codex login status
```

reported `Logged in using ChatGPT`.

Launching the isolated instance and entering `Reply with exactly: TEST OK` produced the same HTTP 401 / `Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...`.

The temporary CODEX_HOME was subsequently removed.

## Direct OAuth-token control test

As a control, I read the `access_token` and `account_id` from the freshly authenticated `auth.json` programmatically and sent them directly to:

```text
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses
```

using:

```text
Authorization: Bearer <access_token>
chatgpt-account-id: <account_id>
```

The response was:

```text
HTTP 400
```

rather than 401.

The test intentionally used a minimal/incomplete request body, so a 400 was expected. The important observation is that the request passed authentication and reached request validation. No OAuth credentials were printed or exposed.

Therefore:

```text
Codex-generated request -> 401
Direct request using auth.json OAuth token -> 400
```

This suggests the OAuth token generated by ChatGPT login is valid and accepted by the backend, but Codex is not using that credential correctly for its `/codex/responses` request.

## Search for reported sk-svcac credential

```bash
grep -RIl --exclude='auth.json' 'sk-svcac' ~/.codex
```

only finds session `.jsonl` files corresponding to failed requests. These appear to contain the server error message itself. The credential was not found in configuration or shell startup files.

## Additional isolation

The normal Codex configuration includes a custom local model provider definition. As a test, that provider block was temporarily removed, Codex was restarted, and the request was repeated. Result: same 401. The original configuration was restored.

The completely clean `CODEX_HOME` reproduction also excludes this configuration entirely.

## Troubleshooting performed

- Logged out and reauthenticated with ChatGPT
- Quit/restarted Codex Desktop
- Verified `codex login status`
- Verified `auth_mode: chatgpt`
- Verified access token, refresh token, and account ID are present
- Verified no API key is stored in `auth.json`
- Verified no `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` environment variables
- Verified no relevant launchd environment variables
- Tested desktop-bundled Codex 0.155.0-alpha.16.4
- Tested standalone Codex 0.157.0
- Temporarily removed custom model-provider configuration
- Tested completely clean `CODEX_HOME`
- Performed fresh ChatGPT OAuth authentication inside clean `CODEX_HOME`
- Confirmed direct use of the resulting OAuth token gets past authentication

## Expected behavior

After successful Sign in with ChatGPT authentication, Codex should authenticate `/backend-api/codex/responses` requests using the ChatGPT OAuth credentials associated with the Pro account.

## Actual behavior

Codex reports that it is logged in using ChatGPT, but `/backend-api/codex/responses` returns HTTP 401 and reports an unexpected `sk-svcac...` API/service credential.

Direct use of the OAuth access token generated by the same login is accepted by the endpoint and progresses to request validation.

## Diagnostic question

Could there be a server-side or client-side credential substitution/routing path causing a service credential (`sk-svcac...`) to be presented to `/backend-api/codex/responses` instead of the ChatGPT OAuth bearer credential?

I can provide request IDs from affected requests privately if useful.

### Summary

Codex Desktop/Work on Windows is repeatedly failing with:

```
401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...
```

The app retries/reconnects several times and then fails.

### Environment

- Windows 10
- Codex Desktop / ChatGPT desktop integration
- Authentication mode: ChatGPT account
- No manually configured OpenAI API key
- No custom model provider or custom base URL configured

### Diagnostics already performed

- `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not defined in the current Windows session.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not defined at User or Machine environment scope.
- `~/.codex/auth.json` reports `auth_mode=chatgpt`.
- `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `auth.json` is empty/null.
- The stored `id_token`, `access_token`, and `refresh_token` do not start with `sk-`.
- `config.toml` has no custom model provider, API key, or base URL.
- The project `.env` has no OpenAI/Codex API key variable.
- Logging out, fully closing the desktop app, signing in again with the same ChatGPT account, and rebooting Windows did not resolve it.
- A reference to `sk-svcac...` in the desktop global state was only found inside prompt history containing the error text, not as an active credential.

### Expected behavior

Codex Desktop/Work should use the authenticated ChatGPT session and should not send or surface an unrelated/invalid `sk-svcac...` service-account-style credential.

### Actual behavior

Any attempt to continue working fails with the same 401 error even after reauthentication and reboot.

There are multiple independent user reports today showing the same `sk-svcac...` 401 pattern, which suggests this may be a service-side or desktop authentication/routing regression rather than a local API key configuration problem.

### Additional note

ChatGPT itself continues to work normally on the same account; the failure is isolated to the Codex/Work path.

### What issue are you seeing?

I am seeing a reproducible authentication failure on macOS with Codex CLI 0.157.0.

Environment:
- macOS 26.4.1, Apple Silicon
- Codex CLI 0.157.0
- Installed via npm/Homebrew path
- Authentication method: ChatGPT
- Model provider: OpenAI
- ChatGPT account login succeeds normally

Symptoms:
1. `codex login` completes successfully.
2. `codex login --device-auth` also completes successfully.
3. `codex doctor --json` reports:
   - auth storage mode: File
   - stored API key: false
   - stored ChatGPT tokens: true
   - stored auth mode: chatgpt
   - model provider: openai
   - provider reachability: OK
   - WebSocket handshake: successful
4. Nevertheless, any actual inference request eventually fails with:

`unexpected status 401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...`

The request is going to:

`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

Troubleshooting already attempted:
- Verified `OPENAI_API_KEY` is not set.
- Verified there are no OpenAI-related environment variables.
- Checked shell startup files and project `.env` files.
- Ran `codex logout`.
- Renamed `~/.codex/auth.json` and reauthenticated.
- Successfully authenticated via both normal browser OAuth and device-code authentication.
- Killed all running Codex processes with `pkill -f codex`.
- Reauthenticated after killing the daemon.
- Confirmed `config.toml` contains no custom `model_provider`.
- `codex doctor --json` reports overall status `ok`.
- WebSocket connection initially succeeds, but the request reconnects several times, falls back to HTTPS, and then returns the same 401 with an `sk-svcac...` credential.

Minimal reproduction after a fresh device login:

`pkill -f codex`

`codex login --device-auth`

Authentication succeeds.

Then:

`codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Say hello"`

Codex reconnects repeatedly, reports:

`Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport`

and then fails with:

`401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...`

This is especially confusing because `codex doctor --json` explicitly reports:

- `stored API key: false`
- `stored ChatGPT tokens: true`
- `stored auth mode: chatgpt`

It appears that an incorrect/stale API-style credential is being introduced during or after transport fallback despite Codex being configured for ChatGPT authentication.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install and run Codex CLI 0.157.0 on macOS Apple Silicon.

2. Log out of Codex:

`codex logout`

3. Verify no OpenAI API key is present in the shell environment:

`echo $OPENAI_API_KEY`

`env | grep -i openai`

Both return no API key.

4. Authenticate with ChatGPT using device authentication:

`codex login --device-auth`

5. Complete the browser/device-code flow. Codex reports:

`Successfully logged in`

6. Confirm Codex believes it is using ChatGPT authentication:

`codex doctor --json`

Relevant output includes:

- `stored API key: false`
- `stored ChatGPT tokens: true`
- `stored auth mode: chatgpt`
- `model provider: openai`
- ChatGPT inference endpoint reachable
- WebSocket handshake succeeds

7. Kill all Codex processes to eliminate stale daemon state:

`pkill -f codex`

8. Authenticate again:

`codex login --device-auth`

Again, authentication reports:

`Successfully logged in`

9. Run a fresh non-interactive request:

`codex exec --skip-git-repo-check "Say hello"`

10. Codex repeatedly reconnects and eventually reports:

`Falling back from WebSockets to HTTPS transport`

11. The request then fails with:

`401 Unauthorized: Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac...`

against:

`https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`

Expected behavior:
The request should use the authenticated ChatGPT credentials and complete normally.

Actual behavior:
Codex reports successful ChatGPT authentication and explicitly reports no stored API key, but the inference request still fails using an `sk-svcac...` credential.

Problem:
Codex was working normally during an existing conversation. Mid-conversation,
automatic context compaction started failing with:

Error running remote compact task:
unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac***REDACTED***

URL:
https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

Environment:

- Windows 11
- VS Code
- Codex VS Code extension (`openai.chatgpt`)
- Authentication: Sign in with ChatGPT
- No `OPENAI_*` or `CODEX_*` environment variables
- No custom `model_provider` configured in `~/.codex/config.toml`

1. Sign in to Codex in VS Code using a ChatGPT account.

2. Start a new Codex conversation and use it normally until automatic context compaction is triggered.

3. When Codex reaches the automatic context compaction stage, the UI displays:

    `Automatically compacting context`

4. The remote compaction request fails with:

   ```text
   Error running remote compact task:
   unexpected status 401 Unauthorized:
   Incorrect API key provided: sk-svcac***REDACTED***.
   url: https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses

### What is the expected behavior?

Expected behavior:
A managed ChatGPT authentication session should authorize remote compaction,
and a 401 should trigger credential/auth recovery rather than repeatedly failing
the pre-sampling compact task.

### Additional information

Workaround observed
Rolling the VS Code Codex extension back to an older version allowed automatic context compaction to complete successfully again.
This suggests that the failure is specific to the remote compaction/authentication path rather than the user-selected model, reasoning effort, or a manually configured API key.

Not collected for this report.

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64; display version 25H2, OS build 26200.9550.

### What issue are you seeing?
The user reports that the Codex desktop application cannot start. This blocks desktop use. The same user also reports many unexpected node.exe terminal windows appearing while using Codex.

Read-only diagnostics found three desktop launch logs on 2026-09-26 at approximately 10:12:11, 10:12:57, and 10:13:23 JST (01:12:11, 01:12:57, and 01:13:23 UTC). All three contain the same bootstrap failure and subsequent updater error.

Representative excerpt from the latest log:
```text
2026-09-26T01:13:23.304Z info windows_core_runtime_component_resolved appPackageCoreActive=false architecture=x64 component=codex consumer=app-server copiedRuntimeLocation=true coreGateEnabledAtStartup=null executablePath=C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\OpenAI\Codex\bin\d23520d1e41bfb24\codex.exe source=copied

2026-09-26T01:13:23.348Z error Desktop bootstrap failed to start the main app phase=bootstrap-import-main
2026-09-26T01:13:23.349Z info [sparkle] in_app_updates_policy_startup_recovery policy=pending
2026-09-26T01:13:23.351Z error [sparkle] Failed to set up updater errorMessage="プロセスにパッケージ ID がありません。" errorName=Error
```
The Japanese error means "The process has no package identity." The updater stack includes Gw.initialize, Kw.initialize, initializeWindowsUpdater, and startUpdaterAfterStartupFailure in app.asar/.vite/build/bootstrap-BmrDl1no.js (installed OpenAI.Codex_26.924.1866.0_x64 package).

The updater error occurs AFTER the bootstrap failure. It is not established as the original cause.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?
On the affected installation, attempting to open Codex Desktop does not produce a usable application (user report). The three existing logs above independently record repeated startup failures. The exact launch entry point and a clean-profile reproduction have not been established. No additional launch/reinstall/reset was performed during this diagnosis.

### What is the expected behavior?
Codex Desktop should open a usable main window. Background helper processes should not create unsolicited visible terminal windows.

### Additional information
A separate process snapshot at approximately 10:31–10:34 JST found a Codex app-server executable under .codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/0.157.0-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/bin/codex.exe, with:
- node.exe running @oai/cua-repl/bin/cua-repl.mjs, with conhost.exe and a node_repl.exe child.
- node_repl.exe with conhost.exe.
- cmd.exe launching the codex-security 0.1.31 MCP launcher, with a Node MCP server child.
- Another node.exe with conhost.exe.
- codex-code-mode-host.exe with conhost.exe.

Several OpenConsole.exe processes started at matching times. Three node.exe processes in that snapshot were all direct or indirect descendants of Codex. This establishes process provenance, but does not map each process to a visible window or prove a common cause for the desktop startup failure and the terminal-window symptom.

Related terminal-window report: #48090 (same daemon release and similar process tree); related startup report: #46764 (different app version/symptom details). Please split or link the symptoms as appropriate.

No processes were killed and no configuration, cache, or installation files were modified. Usernames and private workspace paths are omitted; no raw session transcripts or credentials are attached. Please investigate the desktop startup blocker and the Windows background-process console behavior.

## Update: access restored on 2026-09-26
After the user closed an erroneous Chrome page/tab, Computer Use was retested in the same Chrome profile. The first browser-inventory request transiently failed with `nodeRepl.fetch request failed`, but a native Chrome Computer Use read succeeded. It then navigated through the Helium 10 Ads UI and read the actual Rules & Automation > Keyword Tracker page at `advertising.helium10.com/.../rules-automation/keyword-tracker`. The accessibility tree showed the empty-rule state and Create Rule button. No rule was created or changed.

The original denial occurred during a tab switch. The exact URL active at that moment was not captured, so we cannot establish that Helium 10 itself was blocked. Closing the erroneous tab correlated with recovery but does not prove root cause. Since the intended Helium 10 page is now accessible through Computer Use, we are closing this report as not currently reproducible. If the error recurs, we will capture the active URL and open a new report.

## Original environment and error
- macOS desktop app bundle version: 26.917.51856
- Chrome extension: installed and connected; site browsing set to ask for approval; no custom Helium 10 block
- Error: `This session has been stopped because Computer Use is not allowed on the current browser URL.`
- No account identifiers, private URLs, screenshots, or logs are attached.

Failing: **26.924.20706** (Linux `chatgpt` .deb), bundled app-server **0.158.0-alpha.2**.

Working after rollback: **26.917.71314**, bundled app-server **0.155.0-alpha.16.4**.

### What platform is your computer?

```text
Linux 7.0.0-34-generic x86_64 x86_64
```

### What issue are you seeing?

Existing local Codex conversations remain loading indefinitely in the desktop app after upgrading to 26.924.20706. The user first noticed this around the September 25 service incident, but the controlled version comparison below reproduces the failure without establishing a connection to that incident.

The key result is **upgrade fails → rollback succeeds → reinstall the newer version fails again**, using the same existing conversations and live profile/history databases. No history database was restored from a backup during this comparison.

| Desktop version | Bundled app-server | Result for the same existing conversation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 26.917.71314, before initial update | 0.155.0-alpha.16.4 | History hydration succeeded in 618 ms |
| 26.924.20706, initial update | 0.158.0-alpha.2 | Metadata read succeeds; resume stays pending. Recorded attempts ended after 93.2 s and 208.2 s without reaching `runtime_resume_started` |
| 26.917.71314, rollback | 0.155.0-alpha.16.4 | `thread/resume` succeeded in 106 ms; full hydration succeeded in 346.2 ms; older history pages also loaded |
| 26.924.20706, reinstall/retest | 0.158.0-alpha.2 | `thread/read` succeeded in 1 ms; resume was still pending at least 97.6 s later, and the user confirmed the loading spinner remained |

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On this Ubuntu installation, open an existing local Codex conversation with desktop 26.917.71314 and confirm its history loads.
2. Quit the desktop app and install the official 26.924.20706 Linux .deb.
3. Launch the normal system launcher and reopen the same conversation. Its metadata is read successfully, but the conversation remains loading.
4. Quit the app and reinstall official 26.917.71314, keeping the existing profile and history databases. Reopen the same conversation: history loads successfully in about 0.35 seconds.
5. Quit and reinstall official 26.924.20706 again. Reopen that conversation: the loading hang returns.

The retest used a fresh download from the official package repository; its SHA-256 matched repository metadata whose signature was verified. The initially failing and working installations also passed `dpkg -V chatgpt`.

This is a reproduction on an existing installation, not a minimal reproduction with a new account or empty profile.

### What is the expected behavior?

Previously saved conversations should load and resume successfully after an app update. If resuming fails, the app should present an actionable error instead of remaining on a loading spinner.

### Additional information

Failing re-update:

```text
2026-09-26T03:47:06.023Z maybe_resume_started previousResumeState=needs_resume hostId=local
2026-09-26T03:47:06.026Z response_routed method=thread/read durationMs=1 errorCode=null
```

At 03:48:43.579 UTC (97.6 seconds after resume started), no successful resume/hydration had been recorded for that conversation.

Additional checks:

- Two affected saved transcripts were about 66.8 MB and 92.4 MB. All 7,532 and 8,599 JSONL records parsed, and the history projection offsets matched the complete file sizes.
- An isolated instance of the newer bundled backend, using private copies of the saved data, successfully read both conversation metadata records and history. The larger tested history turn returned 1,493 items (about 8.26 MB serialized) in 314.2 ms. This tests reading saved history, not completion of the desktop's full runtime-resume flow.
- The original failing hydration spans reached `writable_roots_ready` and `metadata_ready` but did not record `runtime_resume_started`. This narrows the investigation, but the exact stalled operation/root cause is not confirmed.
- The older build worked through the normal installed launcher with the normal sandbox. No sandbox bypass was used.

Related reports for the same Linux desktop version: #48212 and #48343. This report adds the specific known-good version, same-conversation rollback/re-update comparison, and timing evidence for loading existing history. Whether these reports share one root cause is unconfirmed.

No conversation content, authentication material, personal paths, or raw unredacted logs are included.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.156.0` today. The menu below was observed on 2026-09-13 while it offered an upgrade from 0.153.4 to 0.154.0.

### Which model were you using?

Not model-specific — the menu is shown before the session prompt.

### What platform is your computer?

`Darwin 27.0.0 arm64 arm`

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

Reproduced in a plain TTY and inside a terminal multiplexer; the menu itself is rendered by Codex.

### What issue are you seeing?

When Codex prints the startup update menu:

```
Update available! <old> -> <new>
1. Update now
2. Skip
3. Skip until next version
Press enter to continue
```

the leading numbers are not accelerators. Only arrow keys move the highlight, and the highlight starts on "Update now". Typing `3` and then Enter does not choose item 3. On two of four launches that key sequence ran item 1 and started the package upgrade in that terminal; the other two happened to skip. Nothing on screen indicates that `3` was ignored.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Start Codex when an update is available, with `check_for_update_on_startup` left at its default, so the menu above is shown.
2. Press `3`, then Enter. Do not press arrow keys.
3. Observe whether the highlight was still on "Update now" and whether the upgrade starts.

### What is the expected behavior?

A menu that prints `1.` `2.` `3.` should select that item when the digit is pressed. If digits are intentionally not accepted, the menu should not look numbered, and choosing "Skip until next version" should not require arrow keys.

### Additional information

Setting `check_for_update_on_startup = false` hides the menu, which avoids the trap but does not fix it for people who still see the menu. I could not re-trigger the menu on 0.156.0 because no newer version was offered during this check, so the observation above is from the 0.153.4 → 0.154.0 prompt.

items.body:
# 问题摘要

Windows 上的 Codex CLI 0.157.1 在共享 daemon 模式中，发送一条纯文字消息也会短暂弹出多个 Windows Terminal 窗口。捕获到发送阶段的四条自动 Git 查询，以及回复结束时的 Computer Use 通知程序；该轮助手没有调用工具。新建 `--no-daemon` 对话的单轮纯文字对照没有弹窗。

关联 #44768（共享 daemon 启动 hooks／命令时弹窗）和 #33254（Computer Use 结束通知闪窗）。本报告补充的场景是：**发送普通消息、没有助手工具调用时，daemon 自动执行的 Git 查询也伴随可见终端窗口**。这可能与 #44768 共用根因，请按需要合并跟踪；本机尚未证明精确源码根因。

## 环境

- Codex CLI：`0.157.1`，通过 npm 安装。
- 操作系统：Windows 11 x64。
- 使用终端：Warp，PowerShell 7；Warp 精确版本本次未记录。
- 闪出窗口所属程序：Windows Terminal `1.24.11911.0`。
- 模型：`gpt-6-astra`。
- 实际处理会话的进程：`%USERPROFILE%\.codex\packages\app-server-daemon\releases\0.157.1-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc\bin\codex.exe`，PID `13884`。
- 用户已关闭自定义 NatsuTerm 命令 hooks 和 prompt-pane Stop hook，但问题仍然存在。独立的顶层 `notify` 仍指向 `codex-computer-use.exe turn-ended`。没有将这些 hook 的禁用状态当作所有运行时自动动作均已禁用的证明。
- 没有额外运行 `codex doctor`；以下来自已有进程记录与一次受控捕获。

## 复现步骤与实际结果

1. 在 Git 工作区中使用普通 Codex CLI 启动／恢复会话，连接共享 daemon。本次捕获来自已经运行的恢复会话，未声称全新配置也已复现。
2. 启动 Process Monitor，仅显示 `Process Create`；另用 `SetWinEventHook` 监听顶层窗口 SHOW／HIDE／DESTROY，在回调中读取窗口 PID、窗口类、可见状态、cloaked 状态及矩形。
3. 发送纯文字“弹窗测试 2”。该轮助手只回复文字，没有执行工具命令。
4. 发送阶段出现四个瞬时终端窗口，回复结束附近再出现一个。

预期：自动 Git 元数据查询和结束通知应在后台完成，不应弹出交互式终端窗口。

## 进程创建证据

以下时间为同一次捕获的本地时间，日期为 2026-09-26，时区 UTC+8。命令仅省略了明确列在表后面的 Git `-c` 参数。

| 创建时间 | 创建者 | 子 PID | 命令 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:36:58.6003312 | daemon PID 13884 | 2800 | `git rev-parse HEAD` |
| 12:36:58.6096903 | daemon PID 13884 | 32064 | `git remote -v` |
| 12:36:58.6183241 | daemon PID 13884 | 33852 | `git config --null --get core.fsmonitor` |
| 12:36:59.5015174 | daemon PID 13884 | 31624 | `git status --porcelain` |
| 12:37:08.3641531 | daemon PID 13884 | 17880 | `codex-computer-use.exe turn-ended`，通知载荷已省略 |

四条 Git 命令均带 `-c safe.bareRepository=explicit`；除 `config` 查询外，其余三条还带 `-c core.hooksPath=NUL -c core.fsmonitor=false`。它们执行的是 Git 查询，不是 NatsuTerm 观察程序或 PowerShell hook。

四个 Git 进程分别创建 `Conhost.exe` PID `31992`、`33308`、`33088`、`29324`。Computer Use 辅助程序创建 `Conhost.exe` PID `2292`。

同阶段系统通过 `svchost.exe` 激活 `OpenConsole.exe -Embedding` 和 `WindowsTerminal.exe -Embedding`。不能把系统激活的 Windows Terminal 伪写成 Codex 的普通父子进程关系。

## 实际窗口证据

下表为窗口监听结果；时间由事件 tick 换算，保留到毫秒作为近似值。五次 SHOW 均实时查询到 PID，`IsWindowVisible=true`、`DWMWA_CLOAKED=0`，窗口矩形大小为 `1248 × 724`，位置在屏幕内。窗口类均为 `CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS`。Process Monitor 中相同 PID 的可执行文件均为 Windows Terminal 1.24.11911.0 的 `WindowsTerminal.exe`。

| SHOW 时间 | 窗口句柄 | 窗口所属 PID | 隐藏／销毁时间 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12:36:59.183 | `0x110368` | 32052 | 12:36:59.507 |
| 12:36:59.199 | `0xA0980` | 32052 | 12:36:59.569 |
| 12:36:59.229 | `0x409A0` | 32052 | 12:36:59.585 |
| 12:37:00.016 | `0x609B6` | 30292 | 12:37:00.258 |
| 12:37:08.873 | `0x11098A` | 33428 | 12:37:09.044 |

Git PID 32064／33852／31624 和通知进程 PID 17880 也出现 `PseudoConsoleWindow` 事件，但这些矩形为零，没有将它们计作肉眼可见的窗口。

daemon 日志同轮记录 `12:36:58 turn/start`，`12:37:08` 回复采样结束。捕获中另有桌面 App 发起的 Git，其创建时间始于 `12:37:00.0229799`，晚于上述四个发送阶段窗口的 SHOW 时间。

## 对照及证据边界

- 重启 Windows 后普通模式仍出现弹窗。
- 同版本使用 `codex.cmd --no-daemon` 新建对话，单轮纯文字交互没有弹窗。尚未用该模式验证全部工具调用或 Computer Use 功能。
- 已直接对应实际窗口句柄、宿主 PID 和可执行文件。Git／通知子进程与这些窗口的时间、数量和控制台活动一致，但没有逐个证明前三个窗口分别绑定哪个 Git PID。
- 尚未捕获对应启动调用的 `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` 等标志，也未对当前二进制定位到具体源码行；不把相关 issue 中的源码分析当成本机已验证结论。
- 原始通知命令可能包含会话内容，因此只发布上述脱敏摘要，不附完整命令行、环境或原始捕获文件。

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.924.20706-1  Official OpenAI RPM package:  chatgpt-26.924.20706-1.x86_64

### What subscription do you have?

PLUS

### What platform is your computer?

Fedora Workstation 44 x86_64 GNOME / Wayland

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating ChatGPT Desktop to version `26.924.20706-1` on Fedora 44, existing conversations no longer load correctly.

The conversation list is visible, but opening any existing conversation causes the content area to remain stuck loading indefinitely.

The same account and conversations work normally in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.

Signing out and signing back in did not fix the issue.

I downgraded the official ChatGPT RPM package to `26.917.71314-1` without changing any other system, network, account, or application settings. After the downgrade, the same conversations immediately loaded normally again.

This appears to be a regression introduced in `26.924.20706`.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Install or update ChatGPT Desktop to version `26.924.20706-1` on Fedora Workstation 44 (x86_64, GNOME, Wayland).
2. Launch ChatGPT Desktop and sign in normally.
3. Open any existing conversation from the conversation history.
4. The conversation content remains stuck loading indefinitely and never finishes loading.
5. The same account and conversations load normally in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.
6. Downgrade ChatGPT Desktop to `26.917.71314-1` without changing any other system, network, or account settings.
7. Launch ChatGPT Desktop again and open the same conversation.
8. The conversation loads normally after the downgrade.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing conversations should load normally when opened from the conversation history, just as they do in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.

### Additional information

Environment:

- Fedora Workstation 44
- x86_64
- GNOME
- Wayland
- ChatGPT Desktop package: official OpenAI RPM

Regression test:

- `26.924.20706-1` → existing conversations remain stuck loading
- `26.917.71314-1` → the same conversations load normally

No account, network, Fedora, Wayland, or ChatGPT profile settings were changed between the two tests.

The same account and conversations also work normally in the ChatGPT web app and mobile app.

The issue therefore appears to be specific to ChatGPT Desktop `26.924.20706-1`.

### What version of the Codex App are you using?

Current installed Linux desktop package: `26.924.22138-1` (`chatgpt-desktop`).
The regression started immediately after updating to `26.924.20706` on September 25, 2026. The previous installed version worked; its exact version was not recorded.
Updating again to `26.924.22138` on September 26 did not resolve it.

Bundled runtime verified with `/usr/lib/chatgpt/resources/codex --version`: `codex-cli 0.158.0-alpha.2.1`.
Desktop log build number: `11645`.
Desktop build commit: `2e782921399a788a842b74ee1944a2e1e6e003a1`.

### What subscription do you have?

Not included in this report for privacy.

### What platform is your computer?

Manjaro Linux (Arch-based), x86_64. Linux desktop app installed through the `chatgpt-desktop` package.

### What issue are you seeing?

The desktop app launches, but existing local project threads/sessions do not finish loading. New desktop sessions appear to work.

The Codex terminal TUI can open older threads normally on the same machine. The affected user has directly tested this, so the observed failure is specific to the desktop app rather than a general inability to access older sessions.

Sanitized excerpts from the desktop logs on September 26:

```text
maybe_resume_started hostId=local previousResumeState=needs_resume vmEvent=thread_resume_requested
response_routed durationMs=1 errorCode=null method=thread/read
name=thread_navigation outcome=failure reason=timeout durationMs=30000.3 threadKind=local threadState=cold
name=thread_navigation outcome=failure reason=timeout durationMs=30000.2 threadKind=local threadState=cold
name=thread_hydration outcome=failure reason=timeout durationMs=120000.2 marksMs={"writable_roots_ready":26.5,"metadata_ready":34.2} startupResume=false
```

Other old-thread read responses also complete in approximately 1–2 ms with `errorCode=null`, while desktop navigation/history loading stalls.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Launch the affected Linux desktop version with existing local project sessions.
2. Select an older project thread/session.
3. Observe that it remains loading and does not become interactive.
4. Compare with opening an older thread in the terminal TUI on the same machine: it opens normally.
5. Updating from `26.924.20706` to `26.924.22138` does not resolve the desktop failure.

### What is the expected behavior?

Existing local threads should load and become interactive in the desktop app, as they did before this update and still do in the terminal TUI.

### Additional information

Closely related: #48208, which reports a Linux desktop regression after an update, successful backend requests, and thread hydration timeouts on Ubuntu. This report supplies evidence from Manjaro and a confirmed terminal-TUI comparison; a shared root cause has not been established.

Additional startup messages include a shell-environment load timeout after 5000 ms and `Git is unavailable` in recommended-skills/worktree-archive handling. Host Git is present at `/usr/bin/git` and reports version `2.55.0`. Whether these warnings contribute to the history-loading failure is unknown.

The logs also contain an unsupported `apps_mcp_path_override` warning propagated as a connection error despite `state=connected`. This warning predates the current regression (see #40412), so it is not presented as the established cause.

No raw log attachments are included. Usernames, personal filesystem paths, conversation/session IDs, request IDs, account identifiers, authentication information, and conversation content have been omitted.
